blocks.x: Cyber & Zero-Trust applied to Capabilities. This page sets out the operating context, the delivery pattern we run, the services and platforms involved, and the outcomes we commit to.

In Insurance & Risk, cybersecurity & zero-trust covers architecture-level security programs: zero-trust network and workload design, identity modernization, threat intelligence and managed detection, cloud posture management, ai-specific security for models and agents, cyber resilience, and the compliance machinery (soc 2, iso 27001, pci dss, dora) that regulated industries must evidence. That is the baseline pattern; the differentiator is what it connects to: zero-trust architecture & implementation, threat intelligence & managed soc, identity & access modernization — delivered on Dataq Sentinel and Dataq Compass with the sector's regulatory posture built in.

items: Sensitive data estate under pressure

Health and financial records concentrate breach value; carrier cyber programs face both attacker interest and regulatory scrutiny on safeguarding. Third-party ecosystems (TPAs, brokers) extend the attack surface.
Claims intake drowning in documents

FNOL packets, medical reports, repair estimates and police files arrive as unstructured documents; manual triage queues claims for days before an adjuster sees them. Leakage and customer patience both bleed in the queue.
Pricing sophistication outrunning governance

GLM-based pricing, telematics factors and external data enrichment multiply model complexity faster than validation capacity. Filings get challenged; model risk documentation is reconstructed under exam pressure.

blocks.x: How we deliver it in this sector

The delivery pattern composes 7 services from the Cybersecurity & Zero-Trust tower — Zero-Trust Architecture & Implementation, Threat Intelligence & Managed SOC, Identity & Access Modernization, Cloud Security & Posture Management as the usual core — sequenced through the Dataq Method with sector controls: IFRS 17 / LDTI accounting obligations shape the design from the first sprint.
Services we deploy in this sector

items: Zero-Trust Architecture & Implementation
Never trust, always verify: zero-trust as an executable architecture, not a slide.
Threat Intelligence & Managed SOC
Detection that keeps pace: intelligence-driven SOC with the boring parts (tuning, coverage) done properly.

Combined-ratio contribution from loss adjustment expense

Model filing preparation effort

blocks.x: Two regimes anchor the control design here: IFRS 17 / LDTI accounting and Solvency II / NAIC RBC regimes. Reserving, capital and model governance under supervisory review. Evidence for both is generated by the delivery itself — control tests, replay trails and documentation are artifacts of the program, not a reconstruction project.

Delivery follows the same weekly rhythm on every program of this type. Weeks 1–2 lock the baseline: the current metric is measured with your team and signed before build starts. Weeks 3–8 deliver the pilot on bounded scope — one decision path, one workflow, one plant or one portfolio — with a control owner named on your side. Weeks 9–12 industrialize what worked: runbooks, monitoring, enablement and a measured delta against the signed baseline. Anything that misses its gate is stopped or redirected with a documented decision, not quietly extended.
